$comment: ★★ ONLY THE `/ENTRY:` THAT STANDS IS A REFERENCE (P69 fold 2, the review of fold 1, NIT 6; D-LK-COFF-READER-SKIPPED-EVERY-LINKER-DIRECTIVE). Two objects NAMED to the link each state an entry: the first is cl 19.44's `/c /O2 /MD /GS-` build of `#pragma comment(linker, "/ENTRY:dss_member_entry") int dss_member_entry(void) { return 42; }`, the second of `#pragma comment(linker, "/ENTRY:dss_archived_entry") int dss_entry_ref_marker(void) { return 3; }` -- and NOTHING in this link defines `dss_archived_entry`. ✔MEASURED 2026-10-10 on these very fixtures (md5 2b93f0bddabed2603b694eae43e437d1 and a12aeb09b00410b879bc390e2f43579e) under a clang 19.1.5 `main`, `/subsystem:console /nodefaultlib`: link.exe 14.44.35228 takes the FIRST entry, drops the second with a warning (LNK4258) and requires nothing for it -- the image links, starts at `dss_member_entry` and exits 42; with the two objects in the other order the entry that stands is the undefined one and link.exe refuses the link (LNK2001). lld-link 19.1.5 requires every stated entry and refuses both orders (`undefined symbol: dss_archived_entry`) -- a link one reference runs is one DSS must link. Until fold 2 a DSS link made the entry of EVERY stating object a required reference as the object was read, before the precedence was asked, and refused this program as link.exe never does (`undefined symbol 'dss_archived_entry'`). The dropped request is said, `K_LinkerDirectiveIgnored`, as link.exe says it. `main` is the witness that the process did not start in the C runtime's startup: it would exit 7. The `release` arm pins that optimizing the DSS half changes nothing: the image never runs it.

prebuiltLibraries.$comment: The object whose entry STANDS: it is named first. Source and rebuild commands: `tests/link/data/pe_directive_entry_member_x86_64_pe.source.c` (cl 19.44.35228 `/c /O2 /MD /GS- /experimental:deterministic /pathmap:`; md5 2b93f0bddabed2603b694eae43e437d1). A relocatable object named to the link is an OBJECT INPUT, linked eagerly, as link.exe links one named on its command line. The witness is the directive itself.

The object whose entry is DROPPED: it is named second, and nothing defines the entry it states. Source and rebuild commands: `tests/link/data/pe_directive_entry_reference_x86_64_pe.source.c` (the same cl build; md5 a12aeb09b00410b879bc390e2f43579e). The witness is the directive itself.
